collection.label: Plato, Laws book 3: the floods and the rebirth of civilization
collection.critical_edition: J. Burnet, Platonis opera V (Oxford 1907), via Perseus
collection.search_terms: plato laws book 3 flood deluge cataclysm survivors mountains origin of government cyclopes troy dorians
collection.description: Plato's account in Laws 3 of the floods that repeatedly destroyed civilization, the herdsmen who survived on the mountains, and the slow regrowth of society from households to cities, on the pages of the 9th-century Paris manuscript of Plato.

texts.title: Plato, Laws 3.676a-679e: the floods and the survivors on the mountains
texts.source: Paris gr. 1807 (9th c.) via Gallica + Burnet Greek (Perseus) + Bury English (Loeb 1926, Perseus)
texts.description: The Athenian stranger on the vast age of human society: thousands of cities founded and destroyed, floods and plagues that left only a few herdsmen alive on the mountain tops, the loss of all arts and tools, and the simple, peaceful and honest life of the survivors, shown on the pages of Paris gr. 1807 that carry it.

texts.title: Plato, Laws 3.680a-683a: from households to cities, Troy and the Dorians
texts.source: Paris gr. 1807 (9th c.) via Gallica + Burnet Greek (Perseus) + Bury English (Loeb 1926, Perseus)
texts.description: How government grew again after the flood: rule by the eldest in scattered households like Homer's Cyclopes, larger settlements in the foothills with the first lawgivers, the city in the plain at Troy, the Trojan War and the return of the exiles as Dorians, shown on the pages of Paris gr. 1807 that carry it.
